This work can be divided into three connected but independent work fronts. The first is monitoring and adjustment: reading scales and instruments on the control panel, monitoring pressure gauges, ammeters, flow meters and thermometers, and adjusting controllers to maintain specified conditions such as feed rate, product consistency, temperature, air pressure and machine speed, adjusting machine or freezer speed and air intake when necessary. The second is startup, loading and processing: starting equipment such as pumps, feeders and conveyors, opening and closing valves to heat, feed in or transfer products, refrigerants and mixes, weighing and loading materials and putting containers in or out of equipment, handling equipment faults such as blockages and notifying supervisors promptly; when frost, ice or frozen material accumulates, removing it according to procedures. The third is recording, sampling and cleaning: entering temperature, throughput and test results on record sheets, sampling to test product characteristics such as specific gravity, acidity and sugar content, checking and flushing pipelines, spraying disinfectant on equipment, and assembling equipment and connecting pipelines, fittings and valves as needed. The three work fronts alternate by shift and production batch, but the basis for judgment, operational risk and responsibility differ; the emphasis also differs across food processing, cold storage and cold chain, chemicals and plasma settings.

Core purpose
Operate or tend cooling and freezing equipment to cool or freeze products, food, plasma or chemicals under specified conditions, and keep equipment running stably with complete records.

Core purpose of adjacent positions: industrial machinery maintenance workers inspect, diagnose faults in and repair equipment; food baking and drying equipment operators handle thermal processing; food batchmakers mix ingredients according to recipes; food cooking equipment operators handle heating and cooking; and metal and plastic rolling machine setters set up forming equipment.
Main objects and basis

Cooling and freezing equipment, refrigerants and secondary coolants, materials and containers to be processed, control panel parameters and record sheets; the basis is process parameter requirements, equipment manuals and production safety procedures.

Objects and basis of adjacent positions: equipment drawings and maintenance records (maintenance workers), thermal processing parameters (cooking equipment operators), recipes and bills of materials (batchmakers), forming specifications and die parameters (forming equipment setters), and chemical processes and hazard information (chemical equipment operators).
Core process
Check parameters → read instruments and monitor operation → adjust controllers and valves → start up and load → monitor products and take them out → record, sample and clean.

Processes of adjacent positions: equipment patrol and teardown repair, thermal processing parameter control, loading by recipe proportions, heating and cooking, and forming equipment setup and trial production.
Main outputs
Cooling and freezing results meeting specified temperatures, stably operating equipment, and traceable temperature and throughput records.
Outputs of adjacent positions: repaired and operable equipment, thermally processed finished goods, ingredients matching the recipe, cooked finished goods, and qualified formed parts.
Responsible party

This occupation is responsible for parameter adjustment, equipment operating status, degree of product freezing, record truthfulness and abnormal shutdown; authorization for major equipment overhaul, electrical work and pressure vessel work is not decided by it alone.

Responsible parties of adjacent positions: maintenance workers are responsible for equipment function and safety status; thermal processing and cooking operators for process results; batchmakers for recipe accuracy; and forming equipment setters for equipment precision.
Collaboration and supervision

Collaborate with upstream and downstream processes, teams and supervisors by production batch, and handle and report parameter deviations, blockages or equipment abnormalities according to procedures; when cross-specialty work (electrical, welding, pressure vessels) is needed, it is performed by the corresponding personnel under authorization.

Collaboration of adjacent positions: maintenance workers hand over faults and maintenance records with operating personnel; operating positions interface with quality inspection and warehousing on batches and samples.
Conclusion boundary

Check against the actual process goal, equipment scope and work authorization; blockage clearing and equipment assembly and connection are Core for this occupation, but that does not mean holding electrical, ammonia-related or all overhaul authorizations.

The preparation levels and qualification requirements of adjacent positions do not apply to this occupation and must be checked item by item against each occupation's official materials and employer systems.
Key occupational judgments

Six recurring professional judgments: whether process parameters and instrument readings have been checked; whether equipment and pipeline status has been confirmed; whether temperature, feed rate and product condition are under control; whether frost, blockages and faults are handled and reported according to procedures; whether records and sampling are truthful and complete; and whether cleaning, disinfection and handover are completed according to procedures.

Before shift handover and machine adjustment, check the target temperature, feed rate, air pressure and machine speed item by item, and confirm whether instrument readings and product condition are consistent; skipping the check and failing to identify a deviation may affect the processed product; the scope of impact and the starting moment must be verified against the actual parameters, product condition and records.

Before startup, confirm the status of pumps, feeders and conveyors and whether pipeline and valve connections are in place, and check for frost, leaks and abnormal noise according to procedures; starting up without confirmation magnifies mechanical and process risks.

Maintain cooling and freezing conditions according to process requirements, and pay attention to product consistency, degree of freezing and the timing of removal; relying only on automatic equipment operation without checking product condition may cause an entire batch to be reworked or scrapped.

Frost, ice or accumulated frozen material must be removed according to procedures, and blockages and equipment faults must be shut down and handled according to procedures with supervisors notified promptly; forcing operation or disassembling unauthorized parts on your own brings personal and equipment risks.
Judgment four: were frost, blockages and faults handled according to procedures

Temperature, throughput and test results must be recorded truthfully by shift, and sampling and testing must be carried out according to the method; missing or distorted key records may hinder process traceability and quality determination; verify the physical items and other materials and do not infer that all records are invalid.

values: Fictional work order materials (exercise inputs)

Fictional scenario: at a fictional frozen food plant, freezing tunnel No. 2 saw two instances during the night shift where outlet product did not reach the specified degree of freezing, while records show the storage temperature deviated upward by 4 degrees Celsius from the setpoint within 30 minutes and then fell back, and the shift record only says 'adjusted'; during the same period, the loading operator reported occasional abnormal noise from the conveyor and a small amount of material piling up at the inlet.

Materials provided: process parameter setpoint table; temperature and pressure records for the shift; freezing tunnel operation and defrost records; loading batch and product specification lists; equipment inspection checklist; summary of safety isolation and shutdown procedures.

Materials not provided: the specific cause of the upward storage temperature deviation, where the affected batches went, the approval process for whether scrapping or retesting is required, and the fault location of the conveyor noise. If the exercise requires these conditions, please clearly write down your assumptions and the parties you need to confirm with.
Task requirements

Please write a one-page night shift handling and operation recovery plan: including parameter checking and exception identification, isolation and judgment of affected batches, the shutdown and isolation order according to procedures, arrangements for defrosting and blockage clearing, conditions for resuming operation, and whom to report to and what to hand over.

The plan should state which data come from the scenario materials and which are still assumptions, and explain whether it relies on the parameter table, temperature records or the inspection checklist.
Reference deliverable (derivable from the scenario)

The plan should include: verification (compare setpoints with actual records, marking the period of upward storage temperature deviation and the batches that did not reach the required degree of freezing), batch judgment (isolate and report affected batches first; they cannot be released merely on the strength of 'adjusted' and must be handled through the retest or scrap process), isolation and shutdown (shut down according to procedures, isolate energy and only enter blockage clearing and defrosting work after confirmation), defrosting and blockage clearing (remove frost and accumulated material according to procedures and inspect the conveyor and inlet parts), recovery conditions (resume loading only after confirming that parameters are back within the setpoint range, the equipment has no abnormal noise and it runs continuously and stably) and records and handover (clearly state the exception period, affected batches, actions taken and items still to be confirmed).
The reference deliverable only lists the elements that should be included and does not require the exact wording of the example; being able to explain the basis for the judgment is enough.
Boundaries and conclusions that cannot be inferred

This exercise only tests parameter checking, exception identification, isolation and record organization ability; it does not evaluate a real company's equipment safety and does not constitute a hiring or qualification judgment or real equipment handling advice.

Do not use a real company's process parameters, recipes or production data; any real pressurized or electrical work must be carried out according to the rules of your company and the competent authority.

description.text: Cooling and freezing equipment operators and tenders (O*NET-SOC 51-9193.00) operate and tend cooling and freezing equipment to cool or freeze products: this covers reading instruments and adjusting controllers, starting pumps and conveying equipment, assembling pipelines and valves, removing frost and blockages, recording temperature and throughput, and cleaning, disinfection and product sampling and testing; it includes the U.S. 2025 median hourly wage of 19.87 USD, the 2024—2034 growth rate 'much faster than average (7% or higher)' and about 800 job openings over the projection period, the mainland China occupation-level wage gap and the industry proxy boundary, and low-temperature and refrigerant risk control plus the boundary of fictional exercises.

subject.summary: Cooling and freezing equipment operators and tenders (Cooling and Freezing Equipment Operators and Tenders) correspond in the United States to O*NET-SOC 51-9193.00: they operate or tend cooling and freezing equipment (cooling and freezing units, cold storage and refrigerators, batch freezers, freezing tunnels and so on) to cool or freeze products, food, plasma and chemicals; in the work they read scales and instruments on the control panel and adjust valves and controllers to maintain specified conditions such as feed rate, temperature, air pressure and machine speed, handle equipment faults such as blockages and record temperature and throughput; there is no corresponding detailed occupation on the China side, and it must be checked separately against refrigeration equipment operation and maintenance entities.
